questions.q: What is the minimum required distance of an elementary school from places of ill-repute, commercial establishments, and heavy industrial zones?
questions.n: DepEd standards require a minimum buffer of 200 meters from busy or undesirable establishments to ensure a conducive learning environment.

questions.q: To prevent the direct entry of sunlight into instructional spaces, along which axis should school buildings be laid out?
questions.n: Orienting the building along the east-west axis minimizes direct solar heat gain on the long windowed sides of the classrooms.

questions.q: What is the maximum Percentage of Site Occupancy (PSO) allowed per DepEd guidelines for school campuses?
questions.n: The maximum PSO is 40% to ensure that at least 60% of the campus remains as open space for assembly and co-curricular activities.

questions.q: For multi-storey school buildings, what is the minimum required Finished Floor Line (FFL) height from the Natural Ground Line (NGL)?
questions.n: Multi-storey buildings require a higher elevation of +325mm from NGL compared to single-storey structures.

questions.q: In a school for 100 male students, how many water closet (WC) seats are required at minimum?
questions.n: The ratio is 1 seat per 100 students, and at least one must be PWD accessible.

questions.q: What is the recommended countertop height for lavatories used by children in elementary schools?
questions.n: 650 mm is the ergonomically recommended height for elementary-aged children's lavatories.

questions.q: How much playground space is required per student for physical education activities?
questions.n: DepEd standards specify 6 sqm of playground space per student to allow for proper physical education.

questions.q: What is the minimum required site size for a central school with 6 classes?
questions.n: A central school with 6 classes (or a non-central school with 3-4 classes) requires a minimum of 1.00 hectare.

questions.q: For most elementary schools, what is the standard height for the bottom of the whiteboard from the floor?
questions.n: The standard height for the bottom of the whiteboard in elementary schools is 700 mm.

questions.q: What is the minimum width required for the main walk providing access from the front gate to the main building?
questions.n: The main walk must be at least 3 meters wide to handle primary traffic flow and ensure accessibility.

questions.q: For a non-central elementary school with only one or two classes, what is the minimum required site size?
questions.n: 0.50 hectare is the absolute minimum site area for schools with the smallest class counts to ensure basic functional spaces.

questions.q: What is the ideal teacher-pupil ratio for preschools according to DepEd standards?
questions.n: The standard ratio is 1:25 to balance educational quality with resource allocation in public preschool settings.

questions.q: In multi-storey school buildings, what is the minimum required height for the steel railings on corridors?
questions.n: A 1.50-meter railing height is mandatory in multi-storey buildings to prevent accidents involving active students.

questions.q: What is the minimum total window area required per classroom for preschools?
questions.n: 10.00 sqm is the required minimum to ensure healthy airflow and sufficient daylighting in instructional spaces.

questions.q: What is the minimum width for secondary accesses (footpaths) between different zones within the school site?
questions.n: Secondary footpaths are designed to be 1-2 meters wide to efficiently connect buildings without being as wide as the main walk.

questions.q: Regarding roof design, which feature is specifically required for multi-storey school buildings but not for single-storey ones?
o: Gutters and eaves at least 1.10m from the corridor
questions.n: Multi-storey buildings require gutters to manage larger volumes of runoff and protect the floors below, whereas single-storey buildings can use trench drains.

questions.q: What is the optimum height for benches used by kindergarten students?
questions.n: 300 mm is ergonomically scaled for the leg length of kindergarten-aged children.

questions.q: What is the standard ratio for girls' water closets in an elementary school?
questions.n: DepEd requires 1 WC seat for every 50 female students to ensure adequate sanitation facilities.

questions.q: For a school with more than 12 classes, what is the minimum required site size?
questions.n: Schools with more than 12 classes need at least 4.00 hectares to accommodate the high density of students and required facilities.

questions.q: What is the minimum required Finished Floor Line (FFL) of a classroom above the adjacent corridor?
questions.n: A 25mm drop is required to protect the classroom interior from moisture and debris from the corridor.

questions.q: What is the maximum height for the top of a whiteboard in an elementary school classroom?
questions.n: The top edge should be between 1.8 to 2.0 meters high to allow teachers to write at eye level while remaining visible to students.

questions.q: What is the required standard for a classroom chalkboard width according to DepEd?
questions.n: The standard built-in curved chalkboard is 4.88 meters wide by 1.22 meters tall.

questions.q: What is the minimum illumination required for classrooms to ensure proper visibility?
questions.n: 10 foot candles is the minimum standard for general classroom tasks.

questions.q: According to green design principles, why is off-white the recommended roof color for schools?
questions.n: Light colors like off-white have high solar reflectance, reducing the urban heat island effect and cooling the building naturally.

questions.q: What is the minimum width for stairways in school buildings?
questions.n: A 1.50-meter width is the minimum to ensure safe and rapid movement between floors.

questions.q: In the context of preschool classrooms, what does 'bilateral fenestration' refer to?
o: Windows on the ceiling and walls
questions.n: Bilateral fenestration means providing windows on two sides of the room to improve cross-ventilation and light distribution.

questions.q: What is the required transom window height above the louvers in a classroom?
questions.n: A minimum transom height of 0.30 meters allows for light entry even when the main louvers are restricted.

questions.q: For boys' restrooms, what is the requirement for urinals if using a trough instead of individual units?
questions.n: 1.00 meter of trough length is the standard equivalent for 100 students.

questions.q: What is the maximum distance a student should walk from their residence to an elementary school?
questions.n: DepEd planning guidelines suggest a 2-3 km walking radius as a reasonable limit for elementary students.

questions.q: A classroom's finished floor line (FFL) for a single-storey building should be at least how high from the natural ground line?
questions.n: Single-storey buildings must be elevated at least 225mm to protect against moisture and minor surface flooding.

questions.q: What is the standard classroom size for preschool nursery classes?
questions.n: The standard dimensions are 7x9 meters to accommodate learning centers and activities.

questions.q: What is the standard driveway width inside a school site?
questions.n: A 3-meter width is the minimum to allow standard vehicles to navigate the site.

questions.q: If a school has 10 classes, what is the minimum site area needed?
questions.n: Schools with 10-12 classes require a minimum of 3.00 hectares.

questions.q: What is the required width for corridors in a multi-storey school building?
questions.n: Multi-storey buildings require 2.50m corridors to handle higher density and vertical circulation loads.

questions.q: Window sill heights for preschool classrooms should be within what range?
questions.n: This range allows students to see outside while maintaining safety and wall space for furniture.

questions.q: Which type of window is specifically mentioned in the standards for classroom use?
questions.n: Louver windows are specified because they allow for controlled airflow even during light rain.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of children allowed per preschool nursery class?
questions.n: DepEd limits nursery classes to 15 children to ensure a manageable and safe learning environment.

questions.q: How many PWD-accessible water closets are required in each school restroom according to BP 344?
o: None, if the school is single-storey
questions.n: Both boys' and girls' restrooms must have at least one seat designed for students with disabilities.

questions.q: What is the required ratio of lavatories to toilet seats in school restrooms?
questions.n: To ensure proper hygiene, DepEd standards require a 1:1 ratio between sinks and toilet seats.

questions.q: The primary access path from the front gate to the main building should be made of what material if possible?
questions.n: A cemented (concrete) surface is preferred for durability and ease of access for all students, including those with mobility aids.

questions.q: Why is a 4.88m wide chalkboard standard for DepEd classrooms?
o: Because plywood comes in those sizes
To provide enough space for daily lessons
To fill the entire front wall
questions.n: This width allows for multiple teaching segments to be displayed simultaneously.

questions.q: What is the minimum corridor width for a single-storey school building?
questions.n: 1.50 meters is the minimum width for single-storey school corridors.

questions.q: For boys, how many detached urinals are required per student count?
questions.n: DepEd standards require one detached urinal for every 50 male students.

questions.q: What happens to the gutter requirement for single-storey school buildings?
o: Gutters are not required, use trench drains
questions.n: For single-storey buildings, properly sloped trench drains at ground level are used instead of gutters.

questions.q: How many hectares are required for a school with 7-9 classes?
questions.n: A school with 7-9 classes requires at least 2.00 hectares of land.

questions.q: In the DepEd standard 7x9m classroom, the '7' and '9' represent what in meters?
o: The number of windows and desks
questions.n: These are the standard floor plan dimensions for instructional space.

questions.q: The East-West axis layout for school buildings primarily addresses what environmental factor?
questions.n: By aligning the long axis east-west, you minimize the wall surface area exposed to the harsh low-angle morning and afternoon sun.

questions.q: What is the minimum height for eaves in multi-storey school buildings?
questions.n: Eaves must extend at least 1.10 meters to provide adequate shade and weather protection for the corridors.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a location from which an elementary school must be 200m away?
questions.n: Libraries are compatible with educational zones and do not require a 200m buffer.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of having 60% of a school site as open space?
o: To act as a parking lot
questions.n: Open space is essential for physical education, flag ceremonies, and student recreation.

questions.q: In the classroom floor plan, why is bilateral fenestration (windows on both sides) preferred?
o: It allows students to see the corridor
It reduces the number of walls needed
questions.n: Openings on opposite sides allow air to flow through the room, keeping it cool without mechanical cooling.

questions.q: A preschool nursery classroom has a maximum of 15 students. How many square meters of playground space does this class require at minimum?
questions.n: At 6 sqm per student, 15 students require a minimum of 90 sqm of playground space.

questions.q: What is the standard width for secondary accesses (footpaths) within a school?
questions.n: Secondary footpaths connect buildings and should be 1-2 meters wide.

questions.q: Why are gutters specifically required for multi-storey school buildings in the DepEd standard?
o: To prevent water from cascading onto lower-level corridors
questions.n: Without gutters, runoff from a large multi-storey roof would drench students and floors on the levels below.

questions.q: What is the minimum Finished Floor Line (FFL) for a classroom in a multi-storey building?
questions.n: Multi-storey buildings require a slightly higher base elevation of +325mm.

questions.q: How much wider is a multi-storey corridor compared to a single-storey corridor?
questions.n: The difference between 1.50m and 2.50m is 1.00 meter.

questions.q: What is the recommended chalkboard height for built-in units?
questions.n: The standard height is 1.22 meters, which is the exact width of a standard sheet of plywood or fiberboard.

questions.q: Which of these establishments would likely force a school to move if built within 200 meters?
questions.n: These are considered 'places of ill-repute' or high-noise/high-vice areas incompatible with schools.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 0.30m transom window above louvers?
o: To provide light even when louvers are closed
To hold a window air conditioner
questions.n: Transoms allow for continuous daylight and stack ventilation (hot air rising and exiting).

questions.q: A school with 5 classes is considered which type for site sizing?
o: Central school with up to 6 classes
questions.n: Schools with up to 6 classes in a central location (or 3-4 non-central) fall into the 1.00-hectare requirement.
